## The Colors of Magic

Fans of the game Magic: the Gathering have long loved my fractal gemstone design featuring the WUBRG-colored moxen at the core of this filigree, ornate wheel. So much so that it got hit with a mass takedown strike during the pandemic. _Well it's back baby!_ You may notice that on Redbubble that it's had some title updates to dodge the lawyers. They can't copyright the very sources that they themselves stole the system from, lolllzzz. I'm bringing it back in celebration of the launch of this website right here. I haven't yet finished designing the backpack, but the dufflebag is up, the playmats are up, mouse pads, prints, coasters, phone cases... you name it!

Big shout out to Marf, my brother Skybreak, MC "Georgie McGregglesworth" Sympathy, I'm a Marf Too, and Patricia of Pat's Games fame ([The Legend on Google Maps](https://maps.app.goo.gl/YtaN83HTD6FSUnYT9)) for all hopping in on feedback for the original design. Peeps have caught me rocking it at MtG tourneys and as I get down on games wherever I travel, I've come across it in the wild time and time again. It's a big top-seller and I've left it dormant long enough.

_It's time again to wake the dragon!_

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/182895224)\]

## Symbol Fractals

Javier Ontiveros, the master who taught me fractals, left a legacy in his passing which was the "symbol fractal" method he created for generating fractal flames. For a while, both Aftermath Arts and myself taught the method to others. . then it fell to myself. My most famous symbol fractal is of course the "[Chaos Clock](chaos-clock)" itself, which now appears on multiple book covers and as album art. You'll find my second most famous symbol fractal -- "Symbol of Purpose" -- hidden away in my [DharmaMix](dharmamix) entry.

I've taught one student after another the method by which to create these. I've since gone further, studying the math itself, then applying it to a new technique that I've been able to extend to Chaotica and even Ultra Fractal. It was this new technique that became the foundation behind the left and right panels for my famous "[Celestial Return](celestial-return)" fractal mural that fans at the Desert Hearts festival and Burning Man have seen. Symbol fractals are easily the largest omission from the main entries that I've covered here on the site.

\[[Chaos Clock on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/20967488)\]

I'll cover a few more right here for you.

## Symbol Fractal: Bangles del Aguila

This right here? It's my absolute BEST-selling design of all time -- especially when it's slapped onto a throw pillow. It's also a massive piece of the puzzle in my award-winning _[Egyptian Turquoise](queen-of-the-nile)_ series, built alongside visionaries like TINY BLVCK, iMeena, and Arike.

The roots of this symbol fractal dig deep into my time out in Santa Fe, Taos, and the high deserts of Northern Arizona. I spent entire summers -- even weathering a few brutal winter months -- living with the Jicarilla Apache and the Navajo. The endless, meticulous hours they pour into their crafts... especially the jewelry and the weaving... it completely changes how you see art. And their use of turquoise? _Absolutely striking!_

Now, I've actually squirreled away an entire feature [here](bangles-del-aguila) on this piece, but due to the amount of art thieves I'm not linking to it from the main menu. It's one of the ways to keep the bots from grabbing it, ripping it, then putting it up for sale. These links below are the only ones you should trust:

## Symbol Fractal: Oz the Great & Powerful

The layered film strips, the incredible rainbow color gradient, and the hypnotic waves that form the eye are all just a few of some of my favorite puzzle-pieces that keep me coming back to this one. "Oz the Great" has never been one of my top-sellers, but instead it's a steady seller that works as a constant reminder of the design itself.

I did eventually release the "silver screen" B&W edition, but it's never lived up to the original. Neither has the "Carpe Noctem" edition in golden film strips. But the technicolor, full rainbow release remains one of the top designs people prefer to pick up on spiral-bound notebooks and hardcover journals.

I sometimes wonder how far those books have traveled... _what words have filled their inner pages?_ In the meantime, you'll find the shattered glass version of this design as the cover for my book "[Memoriam Redacta](memoriam-redacta)" and, if you happen to catch any of these versions out in the wild, I'd love if you would [send me](contact) a photo of it.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23964488)\]

## Symbol Fractal: The Yellow Brick Road That cop must've thought I was completely out of my mind. There I was, fresh off a hitchhiking ride into Las Cruces, New Mexico, taking myself on a self-guided tour through the downtown mall. Suddenly, I looked down and realized what I was actually walking on: a literal trail of yellow bricks winding lazily through the storefronts on either side. A patrol car happened to be cruising the plaza, and the officer pulled up right alongside me. As his window slowly rolled down, the laughter just couldn't be held back. I looked right at him and blurted out, "It's a yellow brick road! _THE_ Yellow Brick Road. Do you know how long I've been lookin' for this?" Either he was too stunned or he just didn't have a script of code to run for the situation. He just stared at me, deadpan, before slowly rolling his window back up and pulling away as he drove past. I still don't know if I made his day... or if I just firmly made up his mind that there's no such thing as a sane bum. The timing of it all was unreal. Just a month prior, I'd been emailing Jeff Grubb -- author of the legendary _Brothers' War_ novel ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Brothers-War-Artifacts-Cycle-ebook/dp/B07C91KLV8/)) -- telling him, "See you soon in The Emerald City!" I was hitching my way up to meet him at the Wizards of the Coast complex in Renton, just outside of Seattle. I didn’t know it yet, but he had a massive surprise waiting for me from himself and J Rob King: an exclusive preview of the book _Apocalypse_ ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Apocalypse-J-Robert-King-ebook/dp/B07BNZ12FZ/)) specifically dedicated to me, my buddy Dragontrainer, and all the other fans (see, "[Others](others)"). It was just one of those wild, synchronistic events that the road always seems to deliver when you're paying attention. Sadly, Las Cruces paved over their Yellow Brick Road and opened the plaza back up to car traffic in 2009. But I'll never forget. Not me. This fractal design goes out as a tribute -- both to the heavy symbolism and political commentary layered into L Frank Baum's original stories, and in memory of that surreal, sun-baked road I once walked. \[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/47474107)\]

## Fractal Feathers: Shikoba

Let's move on to the next glaring omissions -- my fractal feathers! I'm one of the most prolific fractalists in the method for creating fractal feathers. Prepare for a sampling of the most popular cuts.

The word "Shikoba" means "Feathers" in Choctaw. Only the bravest warriors claim the feather of an eagle to call their own. It cannot be gifted, nor given; only earned. In my mind's eye, I saw this as imprinting patterns atop silver, taking me back to my days with Mario and Pops, with a touch of inspiration from leather-working. I segmented the feathers so that the pattern itself clearly emerged, pulling the plumes together towards the middle of the top.

To this day, my friend Teron Solus rocks this as a playmat on his desk when we get together across Spelltable for MtG commander nights each Friday. _Makes me smile each time!_

There's an alternate and highly popular turquoise and tan version of these feathers [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/29316493). However, it's never outperformed the original "Shikoba" -- not in sells, nor amongst the fans.

\[[Shikoba on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/24234962)\]

## Fractal Feathers: Clockwork Dragonfly

_aka, "The Feathered Dragonfly"_

When I first met LiLi Glitch en vrai, she loved the look of dragonflies when seen in art and photos, but their wings caused an immediate reaction to move away from them.. . a gut-level repulsion.

I remember the exact moment this changed.

We were passing through Albuquerque, New Mexico and had stopped for gas. LiLi was taking care of Pocket One, our van, and doing some cleaning. I looked over, down towards where she was reorganizing a bag on the ground. She didn't notice, but an emerald and turquoise dragonfly had landed on her shoulder. A larger one at that.

The woman at the pump next to me followed my own gaze, seeing the dragonfly atop LiLi's shoulder. The woman smiled as LiLi met her glance, then followed to where she was looking, freezing when she saw her visitor. With a smile on her voice, the woman said, "It looks like you've been blessed!"

The Daughter of the Wind held no repulsion towards dragonflies from that day forward. Even that gut-level reaction had gone away. I created this design to commemorate that moment and the blessing that will last a lifetime.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/31910528)\]

## Fractal Feathers: Glowmoth

After "Shikoba", this glowmoth right here was actually my second ever design using the fractal feathers method. I've always loved fireflies. Even before I started hitchhiking, I would walk through fields near sunset where it was as if the stars themselves were dancing all around me. Then I heard rumors that glowworms are a real thing in the Amazon, using their light in caves to lure in other insects... as well as beetles with glowing dotted patterns on them.

So why couldn't we have a moth that glowed with iridescent violet light? I built up the concept from my original "Clockwork Dragonfly" design, completely retooling the palette itself, then finally focusing on the feathers and lighting. Now instead of living as a moth eternally drawn towards the light, sometimes even destructively, the moth itself has _become_ the light.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/34307493)\]

## Fractal Feathers: Autumn Butterfly

On a similar "what if" train-of-thought as the "Glowmoth" from above, I wondered how a butterfly might look if it's wings were made of autumn leaves? Unlike the moth, however, for this one I had to start with the math and build it from the ground up. You see, the leaves had to come first! Only one those were perfect, only then, could I start warping the leaves themselves through Julia variations in the fractal, then finally splitting them and pulling them back inward to form wings around the butterfly herself.

The final effect is startling how much in fact it appears as a butterfly in those blazing orange, yellow, and red fall colors, yet her wings are flayed out in the form of fallen autumn leaves. I one day hope to build this in virtual reality for others to experience in full three-dimensions. One day. Always "one day" . . until the day arrives.

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/57007152)\]

## Fractal Feathers: Da Vinci's Ornithopter

_aka, "Pheasantry"_

It's no secret that Leonardo da Vinci is a major source of inspiration in all my visual works... sometimes even in my life and daily habits. Clockwork gears appear all over my art, mechanical blueprints, and of course... WINGS! As a small child, I refused to believe that I couldn't fly. I was convinced that I just needed to find a place tall enough. I'd jump off the roof of the house itself, grabbing the hanging willow tree when I couldn't fly from there. Finally, I decided to jump from the very top itself. I not only failed to fly, but I managed to hit the one and only fence post with a jagged nail hanging out from it.

This is how you find out at six-years old what the word "degloving" means in reference to the skin that was once "on" your leg.

I've never lost my desire to fly... my love of flying. In the late 90s, I started hanging out at a private airport in West Omaha, Nebraska. I'd earn my way by towing gliders and planes out onto the tarmac with the Geo Tracker on the property. Then I'd fly up in the Kitfox or in a glider. Then came the day when he turned to me and said, "Well, I need a rest. Take the stick for a while." I ended up getting a Glider-A license (along with a B) at that very airport.

Then I started jumping out of perfectly good airplanes.. . and the addiction was final. I'd found something even more addicting than needles. It was an interesting crossroads. I could stay and become a permanent fixture at the airport, just to feel that feeling over and over again . . or I could save it for those rare, precious times. So I left. The only time that I returned after that was for my blood-mother's wedding at that very same airport.

Then in January, 2001, I studied under a lucid dreaming master who taught us the simple triggers used to wake yourself up -- just halfway -- while still dreaming. Loolllllzzzz... omg, the first time it worked, I got so excited that I shouted, "It worked!" Then realized that I'd woken myself up all the way and was now in fact sitting upright in bed with my hands in the air in victory. That's not the right way to do it at all.

Once you get into flying in the Dreaming, you soon after discover "drifting" -- where you simply push off objects and swim through the air... . then soon after came "high jumping" and the thrill of "OH MY GOD THAT'S THE FUCKING GROUND COMING AT ME!!! !" I'd initially sought out lucid dreaming due to a series of repeating nightmares. I actually hated sleep at that point in my life, and while I'm still not a fan, those lessons really changed me. It opened up an entirely new world. I'm lucid more often than not in The Dreaming these days, as it long ago beceme habitual.

And you know what? Flying never gets old. Never.

This one goes out to Leonardo's sketches of ornithopters that still inspire me to this very day. _Thank you!_

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/34685541)\]

PS: My sister Gaea turned me on to the fact that Museo Galileo has the original manuscripts by Leonardo online \[[Main Site](https://teche.museogalileo.it/leonardo/home/index_en.html)\]. Many of these were just recently recovered and/or restored. It's been my favorite rabbit hole to explore for months now!N

## Fractal Mandala: Clockwork Alchemy

This design has been mutating and evolving for years, but until now, the only version to ever see the light of day was at _Da Vinci's Workshop_. If you were out there in the dust at Burning Man in 2015, you might've caught a glimpse of it. Across all thirteen burns I've attended, dropping that piece remains one of my favorite reveals.

I built this using the exact same technique that birthed my award-winning "[Chaos Clock](chaos-clock)". Picture this: you take a standard checkerboard, warp it into a perfect circle, and then multiply that circle infinitely around itself until it bends outward into deep space. It's a notoriously taxing method. In fact, outside of myself and maybe two other fractalists on the planet, almost no one has actually pulled it off.

Mandelbrot originally theorized that gravity either follows or actively creates fractal geometry. It's the reason galaxies swirl into fractal patterns, and why the spacing of stars within a galaxy can be mapped flawlessly using fractal math. In the years since, it's become increasingly clear that if we could just pinpoint the exact center of the Big Bang, we could theoretically map the entire universe.

This specific fractal mandala is where all of that collides. It anchors the ancient symbol of the Flower of Life in its crosshairs, surrounds it with a flawless solar mandala, and then wraps the whole thing in fractal stars and alchemical JuliaN rings.

It is, for all intents and purposes, my own imaginary "Eye of the Universe."

\[[Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/26839128)\]
